relevance_note: The paper describes six families with heterozygous truncating TNFAIP3 mutations, with individually identified patients, e.g. 'a family of Italian ancestry with an affected mother (P4) and daughter (P6)'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON from hand-chosen quotes and checked every span verbatim. Table 1 lists families (one row per family, label column 'Family'), not persons; variants were tied to people through the family label. Supplementary Table 1 (per-patient clinical data) is not in the Markdown, so only features stated in the main text and legends were recorded. Patient labels in the text are only P4, P5, P6 (also 'Patient 6') and P9; Family 1's affected mother and two daughters, the screened index patients of Families 3-5 and the Family 6 mother and her two affected daughters have no labels and were labelled 'unnamed person k' in order of first mention (rule 2 could not give distinct labels for two daughters). Each of Families 3-5 got one row for the screened index patient only; the paper says these families are dominant but gives no count of further affected members. P9 appears only in the Fig. 2d legend; the paper does not say which family P9 belongs to, so P9 may be the same person as one of the unnamed patients (Families 1, 3-6); kept as a separate row with variant 'not reported'. Family 1's 'maternal unaffected family members' were Sanger-sequenced but their number is not given, so they got no rows; Family 2's 'three unaffected family members' got three rows (unnamed person 4-6) with no variant rows. Family 1's dominant disorder 'manifesting early-onset systemic inflammation, arthralgia/arthritis, oral/genital ulcers and ocular inflammation' is a family-level statement and was not attributed to individual members. 'oral/genital ulcers' for P4, P5, P6 was read as both oral and genital ulcers on the checklist. Group exclusions: 'an overt autoimmune disease was only diagnosed in Patient 6' and 'none of our patients have developed lymphomas or other malignancies' were applied to the study patients with TNFAIP3 variants (not to the unavailable sister of P6 or the unaffected relatives); they were not propagated to narrower checklist items. The count 'five patients in our study developed autoantibodies' names nobody and was not assigned. Table 1 gives Family 4 inheritance as 'De novo' but the paper does not describe parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8); maternal transmission in Families 1, 2 and 6 was not inferred, only the parental-testing statement recorded. Variant type is given only where the authors name it for that variant (Family 6 'frameshift'); the group phrase 'three novel nonsense and frameshift variants' was not split by family. Family 1 also had a TNFRSF9 candidate variant, but the paper prints no description and does not attribute it to each person explicitly, so it was left out. P6's elevated inflammatory markers are inferred from 'anakinra, normalized markers of systemic inflammation'. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null: the Methods give 'Seven patients ... NIH', 'four ... Utrecht' and 'two ... Hacettepe' but no stated total. No internal contradictions found; ancestry wording differs between text and Table 1 (Family 1 'Caucasian' vs 'European Canadian'; Family 2 'Italian ancestry' vs 'European American'), both recorded. Protein for Family 2 taken from the text form 'p.Phe224Serfs*4' (Table 1 prints 'p. Phe224Serfs*4' with a space).
